Review: Frey Ranch Harvester Series Third Harvest American Whiskey (2026)

November 18, 2026/David Tao/No Comments
American Whiskey | Featured | Rated A- | Reviews | Whiskey

Review: Frey Ranch Harvester Series Third Harvest American Whiskey (2026)

By David Tao | November 18, 2026 | 0

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:16
Instaread

Back for the third year comes Frey Ranch’s Harvester Series, which is firmly marketed as the distillery’s top-tier release. The company calls it “A blend of our best single barrel whiskeys,” and once again, they’ve tapped freelance master blender Nancy Fraley to carve a path through dozens of mashbills and countless profiles. On a recent virtual tasting, Fraley outlined a bit of what that process looks like: hundreds of samples shipped to her California base, and months of tinkering with some much-needed breaks in between.

In 2024, the inaugural release focused on rye. Second Harvest put wheat front and center. For Third Harvest, Fraley went in yet another direction, crafting a whiskey that showcases triticale, a crossbreed of wheat and rye that’s more often used as livestock feed or a cover crop. Fraley’s blend — officially categorized as an American whiskey — breaks down into the following derived mash bill, comprised of barrels aged between five and eight years:

  • 36.14% corn
  • 27.92% rye
  • 26.66% triticale
  • 4.80% malted barley
  • 4.48% wheat

As with all Frey Ranch products, grains were grown, harvested, milled, mashed, fermented, distilled, aged, and bottled on site. (Co-owner and founder Colby Frey says he plants triticale during the same period as the 2,500 acre farm’s annual wheat, rye, and barley crops.)

Frey Ranch Harvester Series: Third Harvest is bottled at 61.70% ABV and carries a suggested retail price of $300. Let’s dive in.

Frey Ranch Harvester Series Third Harvest American Whiskey (2026) Review

While 2025’s Second Harvest kicked off with a medley of hallmark Frey Ranch aromas — vanilla frosting, spearmint gum, dried alfalfa hay — Third Harvest starts a beat apart. The nose is immediately big on citrus, ranging from orange rind to zested lemon and even pomelo. Early, deep inhales walk right up to the line of cleaning solution, but they (thankfully) never quite get there. Those components get gradually sweeter, eventually settling into candied citrus peel, and perhaps sour berry hard candy. Beneath the bright citrus oil lies both herbs and oak. The former category includes mint, rosemary, fried sage, and lemongrass; the latter is closed to light tobacco. Compared to other releases from Frey Ranch, it’s much closer to a cask strength rye than anything in recent memory.

The palate is an altogether different ride, not absent of citrus but a bit freed from it. Butterscotch and vanilla frosting (there it is!) highlight early sips, and it takes a few tastes for my palate to acclimate to the sweetness. At first, that manifests as decadently sweet lemon custard. Once my tongue catches up, it’s wave after wave of fruit jams on a mix of graham crackers and toasted sourdough bread. By the midpalate, grain takes over, and it’s altogether a pretty memorable handoff between sweet fruit and toasted rye/barley. Spicy pepper and green mint jellies bridge the back palate and finish.

Brown sugar crumble and cinnamon-spiced orchard fruits (pear and green apple) bookend the whole shebang, which generally sticks the landing. That speaks volumes to the blender’s skill, as this one comes close to ending on a saccharine note. But Fraley, with a deft touch, doesn’t let anything get too out of hand.

123.4 proof.

A- / $300
